newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran textile labor said cheapest in region.
newsitem.headline: Honduran textile labor said cheapest in region.

text.p: Honduran textile workers are paid less than those of any country in the Caribbean or Central America, a Honduran labor leader said on Wednesday.

"Honduras is the country with the cheapest labor in the maquiladora industry in the region, being paid (on average) only 38 cents of a U.S. dollar per hour," Hector Hernandez, president of the Unitary Confederation of Honduran Workers (CUTH), told reporters.

Maquiladora is the Spanish name applied to industries in which products are assembled with cheap labor and exported to the United States. In Central America, it applies almost exclusively to the manufacture of textiles and clothing.
After Honduras, Guatemala provides the cheapest labor in the region at an average of $0.69 per hour, Hernandez said.
He did not provide average wages for other Central American and Caribbean countries.
In Honduras, some 75,000 maquiladora workers produce about $1.3 billion a year in clothing and textiles exports to the United States.
